distinguishing_features: Passive metal heat-spreading hardware rather than sensor-based inference and adaptive derating
Reduces local solder-joint temperature rise through PCB thermal spreading and via/copper-pour redesign
Targets cyclic CTE-mismatch fatigue in PCB solder joints rather than thermal-fatigue cracking in a turbine liner
Provides a coupon-based solder-fatigue validation protocol with no new production sensors
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce cyclic thermomechanical strain and fatigue in PCB solder joints by lowering the temperature excursion experienced at the joints without active cooling, operating-point control, or continuous monitoring.
parsed.viable_reason: A thermally conductive spreader coupled to the package and PCB thermal structure is a feasible passive means of reducing local joint temperature rise and the associated mismatch strain, although the assumed 50% reduction must be established experimentally.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying routine thermal spreading to reduce the same thermal-fatigue driver addressed by the closest prior art would be an obvious engineering step.
